subject: Temporary retention window for post-incident debugging — FinHealth
messages:
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@finhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term data hold for post-incident debugging

Hi Tessa,

We had a customer-facing regression last night that looks like it was triggered by a specific prompt pattern. Our engineers need temporary access to token-level traces and the last 72 hours of inference logs to complete a postmortem and reproduce the failure.

Can Redwood grant a timeboxed exception to FinHealth's retention settings (EU region) for debugging? We only need read-only access for a small set of engineers and a secure way to pull the artifacts — ideally a timebound S3-like bucket or transient export.

We can sign any attestation you need and provide the incident ticket (FIN-3457). Please let me know what information you need from our side.

Thanks,
Emily Stone
Head of Platform, FinHealth
emily.stone@finhealth.com
Audit contact: audit+finhealth@finhealth.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@finhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term data hold for post-incident debugging

Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up and sorry you're dealing with this. We can support a timeboxed exception, but we need to scope it and capture approvals. A few quick questions to help us evaluate: 

- Exact artifacts required (token traces, full request/response payloads, KV cache dumps, stack traces)?
- List of FinHealth engineers who will need access and whether they authenticate via SSO (SAML/OIDC).
- Desired retention window (you requested 72 hours; we typically prefer the shortest effective window).
- Confirm EU residency requirement and whether export must stay in-custody or if a transient secure export (encrypted, audited) is acceptable.

I'll loop in Security and Platform SRE to get an approvals path and a plan for scoped access. Attaching our short TempRetentionRequest form helps standardize approvals — please fill and return.

Next steps: once we have scope we will create a HubSpot case and a JIRA for tracking; Security will require KMS-backed encryption, access logs to SIEM, and a signed attestation.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: FinHealth requests 72h retention carveout (EU) — need SOC/security signoff

Team — forwarding FinHealth's request (below). They want a 72-hour exception for token traces + inference logs in the EU region to support their postmortem (HubSpot FIN-3421, Fin ticket FIN-3457).

My proposed guardrails:
- Timebox: 72 hours from authorization (start/end timestamps recorded)
- Storage: EU-only, KMS-managed keys under Redwood's tenant key, no cross-region replication
- Access: read-only temporary credentials, SSO enforce, max 4 engineers (list to be provided)
- Audit: SIEM-ing of all reads, retention of access logs for 90 days, and MD5 checksums recorded
- No long-term exports to FinHealth-managed storage without additional DPA amendment

Questions for Security/Platform: can we implement the above within the next 6 hours? Anything you'd require beyond a signed customer attestation? Also advise if 72h is acceptable vs a shorter window.

Thanks — Tessa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: FinHealth requests 72h retention carveout (EU) — need SOC/security signoff

Tessa — we can approve a timeboxed exception with the following mandatory conditions: 

1) Limit window to 72 hours max, but approval must include exact start/end ISO timestamps and a single point of contact at FinHealth.
2) Data must remain in EU region and be encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS keys; we will generate a dedicated DEK for this export.
3) Access via temporary RBAC roles provisioned through our internal SSO (no hardcoded API keys).
4) All read operations must be routed through our read-proxy so SIEM captures every request; logs stored for 180 days for audit purposes (security ask).
5) Customer must sign the TempRetentionRequest_Form and an attestation stating no downstream copying without prior amendment.

I recommend we avoid shipping full token dumps to customer-managed storage. If FinHealth insists, require an addendum and legal signoff.

Platform (Vivek/Markus) — can you stand up an EU-scoped transient bucket and the read-proxy policy? We can fast-track this under incident response.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@finhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Approved: FinHealth 72-hour EU retention window (conditions & next steps)

Hi Emily — we can grant a timeboxed 72-hour retention window for the artifacts you described with the following conditions (please review):

- Scope: token-level traces and inference logs from 2028-05-08T22:00:00Z to 2028-05-11T22:00:00Z (EU region only).
- Storage & encryption: data will be stored in an EU-scoped transient bucket encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS. No cross-region replication.
- Access: read-only, temporary RBAC roles for up to 4 named FinHealth engineers (SSO required). Tell us the full names and corporate emails; they must be SAML users.
- Audit & retention of logs: all access will be proxied and logged to SIEM; logs will be retained for 180 days.
- Attestation & form: please complete and sign the attached TempRetentionRequest_Form.pdf and return it. Access will be provisioned once we have the signed form and the engineer list.

We will not provide a downloadable token dump to FinHealth-managed storage without executing an addendum. If you need an export to your storage, we can initiate legal review.

Next steps: 
1) Emily: return the completed TempRetentionRequest_Form and list of engineers.
2) We'll open HubSpot FIN-3421 and create JIRA RED-ATT-1886 to track the work and the audit artifacts.
3) Platform will provision the EU-transient bucket and the read-proxy (Vivek/Markus). Neha will confirm SIEM hooks.

Attached: TempRetentionRequest_Form.pdf, FinHealth_Access_Scope.xlsx

Thanks — we aim to have access ready within 6 hours of receiving the signed form.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
